routes.label: Scale the amount and the herd

question: If \(x\) cows give \(x+1\) cans of milk in \(x+2\) days, how many days will it take \(x+3\) cows to give \(x+5\) cans of milk?
solution:
Assume every cow produces milk at the same constant rate. The number \(x\) of cows is a positive integer.

First keep the herd at \(x\) cows. Time is directly proportional to the amount of milk, so producing \(x+5\) cans instead of \(x+1\) cans takes
\[
(x+2)\frac{x+5}{x+1}\text{ days}.
\]
Now increase the herd to \(x+3\) cows while keeping the required amount fixed. The number of cows times the number of days stays constant, so multiply this time by \(\frac{x}{x+3}\). The required time is therefore
\[
(x+2)\frac{x+5}{x+1}\frac{x}{x+3}
=\frac{x(x+2)(x+5)}{(x+1)(x+3)}\text{ days}.
\]
All denominators are positive because \(x>0\). The answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
